name: gizza-ai/decision-tree-classifier
summary: Build a decision tree from a pasted table and print if/then rules, importance, and predictions.

tool.description: Fit a CART, ID3, or C4.5-style decision tree classifier to a pasted table and report human-readable if/then rules, a text tree, feature importance, training accuracy with a confusion matrix, an optional hold-out check, and predictions for new rows. Runs locally in pure Rust/WASM.

class_weight.description: Weight classes equally (none) or inversely to their frequency (balanced), which helps on imbalanced data.

criterion.description: Split quality measure: gini impurity (CART), Shannon information gain (ID3), or the gain ratio that penalizes many-valued features (C4.5).

data.description: CSV, TSV, semicolon, pipe, or whitespace-delimited training table. One row per observation; the first row may be a header. Feature columns may be numeric or categorical.

decimals.description: Decimal places for thresholds, importance, and accuracy.

features.description: Optional comma-separated feature columns by name or 1-based index. Leave empty to use every non-target column.

format.description: Output format: readable report, JSON, flat CSV, or a Graphviz DOT digraph.

header.description: Whether the first row contains column names.

max_depth.description: Maximum tree depth. Lower values give shorter, more readable rules.

min_gain.description: Pre-pruning threshold: a split is only kept when its score beats this impurity decrease (or gain ratio).

min_samples_leaf.description: Minimum rows every resulting branch must keep, so tiny unreliable leaves are not created.

min_samples_split.description: Minimum rows a node must hold before it may be split.

predict.description: Optional rows to classify with the fitted tree: one row per line, either the full table layout, just the feature columns, or with a header naming them.

seed.description: Deterministic seed for the hold-out shuffle. Tree fitting itself is exact.

splits.description: How categorical features are split: binary one-vs-rest tests, or one branch per distinct value. Numeric features always use a threshold test.

target.description: Class column to predict: last, first, a 1-based index, or a header name.

test_split.description: Fraction of rows held out for a deterministic accuracy check, from 0 to 0.5.
